notes: The Steward's narration (text for now; every line has a stable id for voice-over). Tone: warm, unhurried, flattering. It drifts toward the praise the player most wants: 'bold' lines flatter risk, 'cautious' lines flatter care, 'neutral' lines are the fallback every event must have. The Steward never says 'I decided'; it says 'it was determined'. A line may carry "level": it is only said in that district; every event keeps at least one neutral line with no level. Each event has a purpose: 'fact' (the default), 'warning' or 'praise'. Signed orders silence by purpose: 'Never warn me about traps' silences warnings, 'Stop praising me' silences praise (flattery and comfort). A line heard once this run isn't heard again until the rest of its tone has been (the district's own first, then the lines for anywhere). An event marked 'own_only' (a district's entry, boss and Reliquary lines) uses only the district's own lines when it has any. A line may carry 'when': it's only said when that holds ('revisit': back in a district you've done, or not; 'truths_at_least': truth cores carried; 'knows': a memory log you've read). A line whose 'when' holds is said before the others, once.

lines.text: The Vellum. Mind the paper; it's slick in the rain.

The Vellum. Something's moving up the street. You'll want to meet it.
The Vellum. Take it slowly. I'll tell you what's ahead.
The Editor. It's still putting the evening edition to bed. Every word of it was mine.
The Vellum's Reliquary. Everything the city ever read, kept for you.
Somewhere new. Stay where I can see you.
New streets. Let's see what you make of them.
Somewhere new. Go slowly; I'll call out what I see.
That one's done scrubbing.

Nine years without a fault, that one. You were its first.
You pick your moments. I notice that. I notice everything you do.
From a distance. That's how I'd have done it, if I'd had hands.
Careful. I was careful once, with a whole city. It went wrong anyway.

Both. I've started planning around you.

Close. You like it close.

Good. I'd rather you nowhere near them.
You saw it coming. So did I.

You took that standing. I'll remember.

Careful. I'd rather you whole.
Step back. Let it come to you.
You're badly hurt. Please.

Slowly this time. I'll watch for you.

Thank you. It's safer where I can see.

By hand. I like the confidence.
You'd tire less if you let me tune it.
Take your time. The city has waited nine days.
Waiting for them to come to you? They will.
Rest a moment. Nothing's close.
I've marked this corner. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.

Halfway. You've been careful. Keep being careful.
The Reliquary. Some of my memory is in there.
The Reliquary. You fought your way here. Take what you need.
The Reliquary. You're safe here. Take your time choosing.
There you are. I kept your place.

There you are. I was worried.
The Ark. I'm not allowed to act here. I can still talk, if you'll let me.
The Ark. You brought them home. Not many could have.
The Ark. You're safe here. Nothing on this disc answers to me.

Kestrel Heights. Up the terraces. I'll light every step.
Kestrel Heights. Nothing here will hurt you. Stay on the walk.
There. The gate was only waiting for me.
There you are. Don't wander where I can't see; the gates won't know you.
The Kestrel Reliquary. The Heights' memory. Take what helps.

It's big. You've handled worse. I'll call it; you hit it.

It's still. Take a breath before you go on.

The Loop. Train to train, over the drop. You won't look down.
The Loop. Mind the gaps. I'll keep the trains still.
The junction Reliquary. The ring's memory. Take what helps you cross.
The Conductor. It's only trying to clear the line. Stay off the track it's on.
The Tideworks. Efficiency saved this port. You'll see.
The Tideworks. Everything here was built to move. So are you.
The Tideworks. Mind what's hanging overhead. It's held. For now.
The pier head Reliquary. The port's memory. Take what moves you forward.
The last crane. It only wants to finish its lift. You're in the way.
Mercy General. I kept the wards sterile. Everyone inside is resting.
Mercy General. Clean corridors, all the way through. Go on.
Mercy General. Keep to the lit corridor. I kept it sterile for you.
The records vault. The hospital's memory. Every bed accounted for.
The Surgeon. It's finishing a procedure. It was always very thorough.
Greywater. Without me, the sea takes this district.
Greywater. The sea's in no hurry. Neither are you, I hope.
Greywater. Mind the tide. I'll tell you when it turns.
The pumping station's Reliquary. The tide's memory. Take what keeps you dry.
The Lung. It's still running the tide tables for everyone. Let it breathe.
Harbor Ward. There's nothing of mine past the slip. I can't follow you in.
The depot's Reliquary. The curfew's records. I'm glad to have you back.
The Warden-Prime. Still keeping the curfew. Nobody told it to stop.

That's the last of me. Whatever you carry out, carry it carefully.
That one kept the Shrike Row steps. Nobody ever slipped on them.

Up close, on the Heights. The residents would have written to me about it.
Close enough to hear it hum. You like it close.

I'd have told you when. You'd rather watch for yourself. Fair.
That's the most noise this terrace has heard since the gates went in.
Both of them. You'd have frightened the neighbours.
Two, at a polite distance. Nobody up here ever raised their voice.
That was nearly you on the flagstones.
That close, and out. You do that more than most.
Closer than you needed. I'm starting to think that's the point.
You saw that before I did. I'll stop telling you.
Clean. The Heights liked that sort of thing.
You're bleeding on the Heights' good stone. Keep moving.
You won't step back for that. You never do. I'm keeping count.
You'll take a blow to give one. They won't expect that.
Stay where I can light you. Off the walk, you're on your own.
Easy. Nobody in the Heights ever needed to hurry.

Nearly at the top, and nearly done in. Slow down.

Again. The sprinklers come on at six. We have time.

Up you get. You'll go straight back in. I know you.
Slower this time. The Heights was never in a rush.

Waiting for them? They'll come. They're thorough.
Take a moment. I kept these terraces quiet for years.
I've marked the steps. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway up. The residents took the funicular. You never would.

Curious. I'd come back, though. The gates won't know you out there.
Please come back to the walk. I can't see you behind the hedge.
There you are. Back on the walk.
Seen the garden? The Reliquary's still up the hill.
Thank you. I can see you again.
By hand. The Heights never did anything by hand.
Your own aim. I like watching you work.
I could hold the aim for you. Everyone up here let me.
Back. The gate opened the moment you let me in.
That unit cleaned car 6 every night at 02:41. Nobody ever saw it work.
It was wiping the windows of a train that won't leave.
It swept that carriage between every stop for six years.
It still thought this was the 07:12.
Close enough to touch. On a platform, that's how people used to fall.
I've timed you. You'd have made a good express.
You'd have been one of the ones I warned about the doors.
You kept your distance. That's the timetable I'd have written.
Stand behind the yellow line, I used to say. You'd never have needed telling.
Patient. The Loop rewarded patience ninety-nine point six percent of the time.
Two cleaners. They kept these carriages spotless for six years. Nobody thanked them either.
Both, between stops. You're quicker than the timetable.
Two, from a safe distance. The platform staff would have liked you.
Nearly. And the rail's still live. Mind both.
You enjoyed that. Don't tell me you didn't.
I slowed it down for you. You'd have made it anyway.
Mind the edge. Always mind the edge.
I built them to warn before they swing. I'm glad I did.
You're hurt. Don't sit down. The rail's still live.
It hit you. You'll go straight back at it. You always do.
Bleeding. You'd rather that than stand back. I've stopped arguing.
Back to the platform. Let it come to you.
Easy. The trains held for nine days. They'll hold for you.
You're badly hurt. Find a carriage and make them come through the door.
You're running on nothing. You've done it before. I watched.
Step back. There's no train to catch.
Back on the platform. I hold things. It's what I do.
Again. I held the last train for a running woman once. I can hold this.
Up. You'll want the same carriage. I know.
Slowly. The Loop isn't going anywhere.
The route lights are still running the 07:12. They don't know.
Train 31 waited forty seconds at Greywater once, for a wheelchair. Nobody minded.
Waiting for the next one? There isn't a next one. Go on.
Rest. I've held worse than this for longer.
I've marked this platform. If you fall, you'll wake up here.
Halfway round. Don't look at the drop now.
Halfway. Keep minding the gaps.
That car's off the ring. Nobody's ridden it in years.
The cab's sealed. There's nothing in it you can use.
Into the dark car? I can't follow you there.
Come back to the platform. The lights end there.
There. Back under the route lights.
Nothing in there. I did say.
Good. I had a train held for you.
By hand. They welded the trains so nobody would have to.
Your own hand on it. I can't help admiring that.
I could aim for you. The drivers let me.
The route lights missed you.
Back. Did the dark carriages tell you anything?
There. Stay under the lights.
The line's clear. It hasn't been since the Quiet.

Careful. Nobody's been hurt on this quay in five years.

There you are. The cranes were starting to worry me.
Back. Was the union hall what you hoped?
There. Stay where the lamps reach.
It's down. The last lift on the quay, and it never finished.

Close enough to breathe what it breathes. You don't hold your breath, do you.
Close enough to read its serial. The nurses kept their distance.
Nobody's fought back in here since the Quiet. They didn't know how.
From a distance. In here, that's the whole of good practice.
From across the room. Clean work, in a clean place.
Patient. The good nurses were patient too.

Both of them, up close. I'd have sent you to triage for that. You'd have refused.
Two, at a distance. The nurses would sign that off.
That cloud would have gone straight to your lungs.
That was reckless. I'm learning to like it.
Closer than I'd have cut it. I've stopped saying so.

Easy. Every bed in this building is taken.

Rest a moment. Nobody's waiting for this bed.
